watch_list.summary: Running it creates a skill such as /verify-notifications with a formal spec of the properties that must hold, then model-checks possible states.
Use /statechart to visually confirm the generated model matches what the product should do, since only you know that.
Formal checks run in code instead of through the agent, so you pay once to create the skill and save tokens over time.
She uses this on end-to-end flows she needs to prove work, including a Grok Bot bug that spammed phone notifications while someone was already on desktop.
If you forget which skills fit a task, try /poteto-help and ask which ones would help.

items.title: My AI Dinosaur Ran Like a Robot, So I Made It Study an Ostrich
items.summary: The dinosaur's run looked stiff and slow, so he had it study an ostrich's stride and tail balance—using Claude, Seedance 2.5, and Higgsfield Cinema Studio—until the feet push the ground and the body reacts with each step.

items.title: How Two Circles Fixed Where My AI Dinosaur Looks
items.summary: When the dinosaur kept looking the wrong way, he sketched two circles on the frame—stand here, look here—and with an updated prompt the next take went straight into the edit.

items.title: How I Put Myself Into Someone Else's Footage With AI
items.summary: He composites himself into VFX artist Erik's forest footage by asking Claude to blur Erik's head and using his own clip as the identity reference, so the face matches, the dinosaur sits correctly, and the background stays soft.

items.title: Master AI Animation in 3 Steps: Full Beginner Workflow
items.summary: A 47-minute Passport Rush breakdown covering SOUL 2.0 character design, Seedance 2.5 generation, and Blender previs, including failed attempts and how they tighten character consistency, camera movement, and timing.
